title.full: Choosing a private Integrated Shield Plan

summary.text: You do not need one for subsidised B2/C wards in public hospitals. Consider one for B1/A or private hospitals.

details.heading: If you choose B2/C wards
details.body: MediShield Life helps with large hospital bills and some costly outpatient treatments. It is sized for subsidised B2/C wards in public hospitals.

details.heading: If you choose other wards
details.body: If you prefer B1/A wards in public hospitals or private hospitals, you can consider an IP. You should be prepared to pay extra premiums.

Should I get a private hospital plan?
Is an Integrated Shield Plan necessary?

sources.page_title: Do I need a private Integrated Shield Plan (IP)?

quotes.text: You do not need an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) if you plan to stay in B2/C wards in public hospitals which are heavily subsidised.

MediShield Life helps to pay for large hospital bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer. It is sized for subsidised treatment in B2/C wards of the public hospitals.

However, if you are firm in choosing B1/A wards in public hospitals or seeking treatment at private hospitals, you can consider getting an IP that matches your ward preference. If so, you should be prepared to pay additional premiums for the additional coverage.
